content: Bacitracin should be administered exclusively via intramuscular injection. For infants weighing less than 2500 grams, the recommended dosage is 900 units per kilogram of body weight per 24 hours, divided into two or three doses. For infants weighing more than 2500 grams, the dosage is 1000 units per kilogram of body weight per 24 hours, also divided into two or three doses. Intramuscular injections should be administered in the upper outer quadrant of the buttocks. It is important to alternate between the right and left sides to avoid repeated injections in the same area, as this can cause transient pain following the injection. The preparation of bacitracin solutions requires dissolving the antibiotic in sodium chloride injection that contains 2% procaine hydrochloride. The final concentration of bacitracin in the solution should be between 5000 units per milliliter and 10,000 units per milliliter. Diluents containing parabens must not be used to reconstitute bacitracin, as they have been associated with the formation of cloudy solutions and precipitates. To achieve a concentration of 5000 units per milliliter, 8 milliliters of diluent should be used. Before administration, parenteral drug products should be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration, provided that the solution and container allow for such inspection.
